svg.title: Voltstream data flow: where a meter reading goes
svg.desc: Data flow of the Voltstream Lambda pipeline. meter-producer publishes readings to the Kafka topic meter.readings (3 partitions, keyed by household_id). Two consumers read it independently: raw-archiver appends every record unchanged to Parquet in MinIO bucket voltstream-raw, and speed-layer runs three Spark Structured Streaming queries that upsert zone_metrics_rt and household_running_rt in Postgres and send rejected records to rejected_records and the meter.readings.dlq topic, which nothing consumes. reference-dropper writes tariff_D.csv to voltstream-landing when day D closes; the speed layer prices day D with the previous day's tariff, and the file's arrival triggers the Airflow daily_billing DAG, whose containers rescan the day from voltstream-raw and write pipeline_runs, household_bill_daily, household_bill_history, zone_metrics_daily and reconciliation_daily, plus an archived tariff and report in voltstream-archive. The weather file is written but never read. voltstream-api reads Postgres and merges: the batch bill if the day is finalised, otherwise the speed estimate; the dashboard polls it every 5 seconds.
svg.text: Every arrow is a read or a write in the code. Colour says which layer owns the data; F1–F6 are the injected faults in diagram 4.
per day · priced with tariff D−1
static files served by the API
tariff_D.csv arrives = day D is closed → triggers daily_billing, which prices D with it
